name: Closed Eyes
description: A pad and keys that tire as you hold them: each note pales while it is looked at, and when you let it go its opposite appears and floats away.

params.name: Source
params.description: What is looked at: a glowing lamp, a reed, a rubbed bowl, a sung vowel, a struck bar or bell, or a plucked string. Heard from the next key.

params.name: Opposite
params.description: What is left behind: even partials, the note across the keyboard, its two trembling sides, torn bands, breath in waves, or a hollow octave below.

params.name: Form
params.description: The shape of the source: hollow to octaves, thin to full reed, dark to bright rim, oo to ee, wood to bell to glass, a string from wiry and long to hollow and short.

params.name: Colour
params.description: How bright the source is, and how dark its opposite: what is bright tires in its upper partials too, and leaves a rounder outline behind.

params.name: Air
params.description: Breath and contact round the source: hiss in the lamp and the voice, the bow of the bowl, the mallet, the finger on the string.

params.name: Attack
params.description: How slowly a key blooms. A quick one also speaks with a brighter beginning. Struck bars and strings are far sooner, and only soften.

params.name: Release
params.description: How long the note itself takes to fall away when its key is let go. Short leaves the opposite bare; long lets the two overlap. Bowls and voices take longer.

params.name: Tire
params.description: How long a held note takes to tire. The more it has tired when it is let go, the stronger its opposite.

params.name: Depth
params.description: How far a tired partial sinks. The strong ones tire most, so a held note pales and thins; at the top mostly what was faint is left.

params.name: Recover
params.description: How long a pitch stays tired after it was held. A key that returns sooner comes back paler, with its opposite already showing.

params.name: Memory
params.description: What tires together: each key alone, the same note in every octave, or everything held, so a full chord tires sooner than one key.

params.name: After Level
params.description: How loud the opposite is against the note that left it. At zero there is none.

params.name: After Length
params.description: How long the opposite takes to fade once it is seen. The bells of Mirror go in about half of it, breath and bands a little sooner.

params.name: After Rise
params.description: How slowly the opposite comes up when the note goes: at once like a flash, or later, out of the silence.

params.name: Edge
params.description: How sharp the opposite's outline is: round and dark, or bright, with rougher bands and more hiss where it has them.

params.name: Seep
params.description: How much of the opposite already shows through while the key is held. As the note tires it gives way to it.

params.name: Drift
params.description: How much everything floats: note and opposite swell partial by partial, and the opposite's pairs part in pitch and beat.

params.name: Blink
params.description: Closes the eyes again and again while keys are held: each time the note goes dark and its opposite flashes. Tired notes rest a little meanwhile.

params.name: Blink Rate
params.description: How often the eyes close when Blink is up: from a slow change of light to a flutter. All keys blink together.

params.name: Safe
params.description: With Move an opposite that lingers under a new chord crosses over to the nearest tone that is held. With Stay it keeps its own.

params.name: Width
params.description: How far note and opposite spread to the sides. The lowest partial stays near the middle; the two sides and the torn bands go widest.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Overall output level of the instrument.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. After sensory adaptation and opponent colour: each partial carries a slow state that takes itself away from the sound and drives an opposite bank when the note stops. Spectra are closed forms voiced by measurement; mode ratios of bar, bell and glass are textbook values.
